title: Handle a duplicate key deliberately
summary: ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE changes a row when an insert meets an existing unique key.
introduction: ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE changes a row when an insert meets an existing unique key. Your task: Explain why only one Mia row remains.
learningObjectives: Explain why only one Mia row remains.
Explain the example for handle a duplicate key deliberately

blocks.text: ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE changes a row when an insert meets an existing unique key. The matching key decides which row is affected.

Use MariaDB 10.11+ with its mariadb client in an empty practice database. These dialect-specific examples do not run in the site's SQLite playground. Keep the sample database separate from real records.

blocks.title: Handle a duplicate key deliberately

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: A primary key identifies a row and prevents duplicate key values. Related records can refer to that key.
The duplicate-key clause changes the row matched by a unique-key conflict rather than creating a second conflicting row.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.text: Mia's points become 5 rather than creating a second row with the same key.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Understand every unique key on a real table. A duplicate match can happen on more than the primary key.
